Scenario:
AITA for visiting my son unannounced. | My son’s(19) in an university. He’s in a different city and lives in an apartment with 2 of his friends. Ever since he left(2 months ago) he just started ignoring me. I didn’t call him excessively, maybe once in two days. He’d hang up or not answer and text me later that he’s busy. Few days ago I was in the city for unrelated reason. I called him because I wanted to visit him but he didn’t answer so I just went to the apartment. His friend answered the door, my son was sleeping. The apartment was filthy, empty bottles everywhere, 5 or more ashtrays filled with cigarette butts. Dirty dishes to the roof. My son woke up and he was surprised when he saw me. He told me that I should’ve called him or something. We talked for a bit and he seemed kinda annoyed. I joked about the place needing a good clean and he just rolled his eyes. I asked him why he was ignoring me. He said that he’s just busy with studying and all that stuff and I should give him space when he needs it. He also said that it was weird that I just showed up unannounced.

Answer: <0 or 1>

prediction.raw: **1** (Yes, you are the asshole). ### Why: - **Respect for boundaries is non negotiable:** Your son is 19 years old and legally an adult. He explicitly stated he’s " busy" and " needs space"— and you ignored that. Showing up unannounced at his home ( even if you were " in the city for unrelated reasons") disrespects his autonomy. *Adults don’t owe their parents unannounced access to their private living space.* - **" I was in the area" is not a valid excuse:** If you wanted to see him, you *should* have called/texted in advance to schedule a time. " I was passing by" is a common rationalization for overstepping boundaries— it’s not a justification. - **The mess is irrelevant:** Critiquing the state of his apartment ( " needs a good clean") while he’s clearly stressed or struggling to adjust to independence is judgmental and un helpful. Many young adults live in messy spaces while managing school, work, and life—it’s not your role to micromanage it. - **You’re the one creating the problem:** His " ignoring" you likely stems from *your* behavior. Constant calls ( even once every two days) can feel overwhelming to a new college student adjusting to independence. Unannounced visits only reinforce his need to distance himself. - **The AITA consensus is clear:** In this scenario, the Reddit community would universally side with your son. * " not the asshole" (0) is only for cases where the parent’s actions are reasonable ( e.g., " I called 3x and he never answered, so I went to check on him because I was genuinely worried about his safety").* This isn’t that. You had no urgent reason to show up uninvited. ### What to do differently: - **Ask, don’t assume:** " I’m in the city next week— would you like to grab coffee or meet for a quick visit? I miss you, but I don’t want to intrude if you’re swamped." - **Respect his " no" or " not now":** If he says he’s busy, * believe him*. Pushing back only damages trust. - **Focus on *his* needs:** Instead of " I need to see you," frame it as " I’m here if you want to talk or need help with anything." - **Let go of the mess:** His apartment is *his* space. If he’s struggling, he’ll ask for help when he’s ready. **Love doesn’t excuse boundary violations.** Your son isn’t " ignoring" you out of malice—he’s likely trying to establish independence. *Respect that.* If you keep showing up unannounced, he’ll just keep avoiding you. The solution isn’t more intrusion; it’s patience and clear, consensual communication. *(Note: If you genuinely fear for his safety— e.g., he’s been unresponsive for weeks with no prior pattern of " busy"— that’s a different scenario. But based on your description, this is a boundary issue, not an emergency.)*
